children: Bank of America Securities is warning investors that the stock market's
primary drivers—positioning, profits and policy—are peaking, signaling a structural market rotation is already underway.

Market positioning is "too bullish," BofA reiterated in its latest Flow Show note, with the Bull & Bear Indicator triggering a 9.5 sell signal again and fund-manager positioning hitting the 100th percentile. Moreover, a record net 33% of fund managers now report companies are overinvesting.
Concurrently, profit expectations are moderating into 2027 as "GDP boom hopes are over," while monetary policy has
from a "run it hot" posture, requiring higher bond
The macro shift is actively driving sector rotation. Since the Nasdaq's
peak on June 1st, rising Federal Reserve hike expectations have deflated early leaders, specifically AI
and independent power producers, the note said.
For investors, BofA outlined a specific playbook: while it is "not yet time for defensives," a pivot toward quality
, and yield looks prudent. However, the firm cautions that current market winners—commodities, credit and China bonds—represent key vulnerabilities heading into the fourth quarter.

title: Market's '3 Ps are all peaking' as rotation takes hold - BofA
